Contributing guidelines

  • I have read CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

Module(s)

mini.completion

Question

Hello,

I've setup mini.keymap, mini.snippets and mini.completion (along with most modules) and enabled the examples configuration to get <Tab>/<S-Tab> to select completion entries and signature tabstops. It works fine with Return too. I love it.

I just wonder if it's still possible that Tab can also work with a completion session and completing fields poping up while editing a placeholder. Currently in my case it goes to the next parameter if the session is open.

Example:

Enregistrement.de.l.ecran.2026-04-20.090051.mp4

When I try to expand ex. to get access to fields of example struct, it goes to the next parameter. In that case and are okay though but obviously I tend to hit Tab first now that I'm used to.

Is there something I need to add? Is it doable?

Here's my entire configuration:

comment_data.body:
Hmm, actually I think this could be confusing because if you don't want the menu to complete and jump to the next placeholder, you will end up in the menu list rather than the next stop.

I think I'll stick to `<C-N>/<C-P>` to select menu items and only use `<Tab>/<S-Tab>` to navigate between tabstops. However, I wonder what are the user common mappings for such scenarios and how they manage their completion sessions?

comment_data.body:
The reason for this behavior is described in the config itself:

```lua
--
-- Allow <Tab>/<S-Tab> to select placeholders while completion is active or
-- use the pmenu completion instead.
--
mini.keymap.map_multistep("i", "<Tab>", {
    "minisnippets_next",
    "minisnippets_expand",
    "pmenu_next"
})

mini.keymap.map_multistep("i", "<S-Tab>", {
    "minisnippets_prev",
    "pmenu_prev",
    "jump_before_tsnode",
    "jump_before_open",
})
```

It is set up in a way that prefers jumping through snippet even if there is an active completion. Adjusting the order of steps should help here:

```lua
mini.keymap.map_multistep("i", "<Tab>", {
    "pmenu_next",
    "minisnippets_next",
    "minisnippets_expand",
})

mini.keymap.map_multistep("i", "<S-Tab>", {
    "pmenu_prev",
    "minisnippets_prev",
    "jump_before_tsnode",
    "jump_before_open",
})
```

> Hmm, actually I think this could be confusing because if you don't want the menu to complete and jump to the next placeholder, you will end up in the menu list rather than the next stop.

This can be resolved by explicitly ending completion (either with `<C-e>` or `<C-y>`) and *then* pressing `<Tab>` or `<S-Tab>`.

> I think I'll stick to `<C-N>/<C-P>` to select menu items and only use `<Tab>/<S-Tab>` to navigate between tabstops. However, I wonder what are the user common mappings for such scenarios and how they manage their completion sessions?

[`<Tab>` and `<S-Tab>` only for completion navigation](https://github.com/nvim-mini/MiniMax/blob/c84e697595116e6c2a1a2cf13afe47b832283d48/configs/nvim-0.12/plugin/30_mini.lua#L547-L552) and [snippet navigation with default `<C-l>` and `<C-h>`](https://github.com/nvim-mini/MiniMax/blob/c84e697595116e6c2a1a2cf13afe47b832283d48/configs/nvim-0.12/plugin/30_mini.lua#L728-L735).
